_readme: Map danger warnings, feature discovery, territory-change gossip and Territory notices (Saga), v1. Rules from docs/design/world-map-territory-v0.1.md at 769cbed (v0.1.5: four danger levels, single highest hazard, never the sum). Hazard ids from map-v1 and map.json, plus humans and hyenas from map section 10. Claim words from my-pride v0.1.2 and cat-directory-copy-v1.json. Voice: narrator-voice-v1.md, second person present for narrator lines, no digits or number words, no game words, no saber colour, no pronouns for a single other cat. Director: common knowledge says only that humans and hyenas roam the far edges; this bank must not name a camp or den location until the player knows it. Selection: each list is tried in order, the first matching when wins, and the last entry has no when and is the default. At least three variants per key. Does not repeat region-arrivals-v1 landscape or lore-book-copy-v1 encyclopedia lines.

_tokens.sourceName: The cat who told the player about a feature.
_tokens.holderName: The pride (or pack) that holds, or has just taken, the region.
_tokens.loserName: The pride that lost the region.
_tokens.rivalName: The challenging pride, on contested (and lost-to) lines. Same token as the My Pride header.
_tokens.name: A known cat, usually the leader who took or marked the ground. Only on leaderKnown lines.

_schema.when: First match wins; the last entry in a list has no when and is the default. Matches if every key present is true. hazard is a known hazard id (humans, hyenas, or a map-v1 id). change is taken, claimed, lost, wild or contested. side is player_gained, player_lost or player_contested. sociability is the teller's band (high / low; baseline is the unbanded default). leaderKnown is true only when {name} can be filled. claim is strong, held, slipping, contested, lost or lost_unclaimed, and contested wins.
_schema.danger: unknown, then levels safe 0, uneasy 1, dangerous 2, deadly 3. Each has a short tooltip and a travel list. Travel is tried in hazard order, then the default.
_schema.features: human_camp and hyena_den, each with visit, scent, gossip and repeat. Gossip requires {sourceName} and {zoneName}.
_schema.territory_gossip: Every line is kind holder_change. Player-pride news is selected by side, then other-pride news, then the default.
_schema.notices: patrol_due and scent_fading, each with the approved short label and a when.claim list.

_gaps: No dedicated lines for a band-held stretch (map-v1, bandHeld). Ordinary taken, claimed, lost, wild or contested lines can still play if the names fill.
No dedicated lines for a dire-wolf holder change. Wolves are a static holder in v1, so this should not come up; {holderName} will still read if it ever does.
No council-flavoured cession lines for a border deal. A deal that changes a holder can use taken, lost or claimed as written.
No extra travel variants for danger raised only by trespass or by a band's range, with no known land or beast hazard. The level default covers those.
Patrol-due is written for strong, held, slipping and contested, which are the words used on held Territory lines. There is no patrol-due line for Lost.
Tundra ccdba1c: contested gossip keeps {rivalName}; {loserName} is for taken and lost only. Patrol-due never shows on Lost ground; that ground just reads Lost, since winning it back is a Mark.

Flint: travel gets the known hazard that set the level (ties go to map.json order); a known camp or den arrives as a separate feature key. Flint passes catId and fills {name}; leaderKnown stays the when gate for {name} lines.
_questions: Ochre: tooltips are short panel lines; travel, features, notices and the default territory lines are ordinary upright narrator colour. Territory gossip with a teller can sit in the npc colour, with {sourceName} only in the feature-gossip beats, which are narrator-framed.

danger._note: Labels from map territory 3.2 (Saga's words). Danger is the band of the region's single highest known daily hazard, plus known trespass, band range, or a known camp or den, clamped to the four levels. Unknown is shown when the player has no such facts. Tooltips sit on the region panel before travel. Travel lines play when the cat goes in. Hazard variants fire only if that hazard is already known; pass the known hazard that set the band, or walk this list in order (first when match wins). Default travel never names humans, hyenas, a camp or a den.

variants.text: You walk into {zoneName} without knowing what waits there.
The ground ahead is unfamiliar, and you have no warning to go by.
You enter {zoneName} in the dark, as far as danger goes. Keep your ears up.
Upright walkers have used {zoneName}, though the land still feels easy. You keep downwind of any smoke.
There has been fire-scent at {zoneName}, the kind humans leave. The walking is quiet now, but you do not forget it.
Humans have passed this ground. Nothing stirs as you enter, and still you watch the open approaches.

You enter {zoneName} with tar in mind. The walking is quiet if you pick your path, and you pick it with care.
Loose stone lies under the walls at {zoneName}, though nothing is falling now. You still keep an ear on the rock.
The cliffs at {zoneName} have shed stone before. The walking feels easy, and you do not linger at the foot of them.
You enter {zoneName} under quiet rock. A little dust in the air is enough to make you choose the wider path.
The water at {zoneName} is louder than usual, though the banks still hold. You keep to the higher ground as you come in.
Melt-scent and wet earth hang at {zoneName}. The walking is easy on the rise, and you do not trust the lowest path.
You enter {zoneName} with rising water in mind. Nothing has spilled over yet, and you choose the upper trail anyway.
A harder cold is in the air at {zoneName}, though you can walk it well enough. You keep moving so it does not settle in.
The wind at {zoneName} has a metallic bite. The ground feels easy, and you would still rather not sleep in the open here.
You enter {zoneName} in a sharpening cold. Nothing else warns you, so you listen to that.
Prey-scent is thin at {zoneName}, though the walking feels easy. You will not grow fat here, and you do not expect to.
The ground at {zoneName} is poor in food-smell. Nothing else troubles you, so hunger is the thing to watch.
You enter {zoneName} on hungry ground that is otherwise quiet. Hunt if you must, and do not spend yourself on empty trails.
The trails at {zoneName} wander and cross, though you can still read them today. You keep a landmark in mind.
A little fog blurs the paths at {zoneName}. The walking feels easy, and you still glance back the way you came.
You enter {zoneName} on ground that likes to turn a cat around. Nothing worse waits, so long as you keep your bearings.
You walk into {zoneName}, and the land lies easy under your paws.
Nothing here sets your fur on end. The walking is quiet.
The air at {zoneName} carries no warning. You go on without hurrying.
You enter {zoneName} with the scent of fire in mind. Humans keep to this ground, and their sticks wound from far off.
Upright walkers roam {zoneName}. You come in low, watching for smoke and for shapes that do not move like beasts.
There are humans on this ground. No cat can fight them, so you walk it carefully and keep a way out.
You enter {zoneName} with hyena-scent in mind. A clan dens on this ground, and they will take a meal if they can.
Scavenger tracks cross {zoneName}. You come in watching the downwind side, where a hyena clan likes to wait.
Hyenas keep to this ground. You walk it with your meal in mind, and you do not settle with meat in the open.
You enter {zoneName} with bear-scent in mind. Something that large does not need to hurry.
A short-faced bear uses this ground. You come in quietly and keep a way out of the rocks.
Bear-scent clings to {zoneName}. You walk it with your head up, and you do not linger in the narrow places.
You enter {zoneName} with wolf-scent in mind. A pack hunts this ground, and you keep your ears on the downwind side.
Pack-sign crosses the trail into {zoneName}. You come in watching, and you do not linger over a meal.
Wolves use this ground. You walk it carefully and keep a catch close, if you are carrying meat.
Snow hangs heavy above the trail into {zoneName}. You cross it without a wasted sound.
The slope above {zoneName} has a waiting look. You go in lightly, ready to move if the snow answers.
You enter {zoneName} with an ear on the high snow. A wrong sound could bring it down.

You enter {zoneName} knowing the ice can lie. What holds at the edge may not hold farther out.
The ice at {zoneName} wants watching. You go in with a path back to solid ground already chosen.

You enter {zoneName} knowing the river can spread without warning. You keep a dry path in mind.

The cold at {zoneName} has a bite that stings the nose. You come in already thinking of shelter.
You enter {zoneName} knowing a bitter cold can close on this ground. You do not linger in the wind.

Prey-scent is thin and old at {zoneName}. You come in knowing a cat can go hungry here.

You enter {zoneName} knowing the ground can turn you around. You keep the wind, or a tree, or a stone, and you hold to it.
You enter {zoneName} with your ears up. Something here wants watching.

You walk into {zoneName} knowing hyenas den here. Their stink is a warning, and a whole clan will take a meal from under you.

You walk into {zoneName} knowing a short-faced bear haunts this ground. You go in ready to move, and you do not look for a fight.

A bear is on this ground. You keep to the wider approaches and you do not settle.
You walk into {zoneName} knowing a pack hunts here. Wolf-scent is heavy, and this ground can cost you a meal, or your hide.

You walk into {zoneName} knowing the high snow can take a cat. Every step is placed as if the slope were listening.

You walk into {zoneName} knowing the ice has taken cats. Every step is a question, and you listen for the hollow answer.

You walk into {zoneName} knowing the seeps can hold a cat. There is prey-scent too, and that is how they catch the hungry.

The walls at {zoneName} shed stone without warning. You go through fast and you do not rest at the foot of them.
You walk into {zoneName} knowing the rock can come down. Every open stretch under a cliff is a place to leave, not to linger.
Loose scree and raw scars on the stone mark {zoneName} as ground that hurts from above. You keep moving.
The water at {zoneName} has already taken the low ground. You go in along whatever rise is left, and you do not dawdle in the wet.

Melt and mud have remade the trails at {zoneName}. You keep to high ground, or you turn back.
The cold at {zoneName} can kill a still cat. You go in, you keep moving, and you look for shelter before you look for prey.
You walk into {zoneName} with the air burning in your chest. This ground can hurt you without using teeth.
A bitter snap has hold of {zoneName}. You do not hunt at leisure here, and you do not rest in the open.
There is almost no food-smell at {zoneName}, only old bones. You go in knowing this ground can weaken you, and a weak cat is easy prey.
You walk into {zoneName} on starving ground. If you hunt here, you may spend more than you catch.
The land at {zoneName} is bare. Hunger is the danger, and it will catch any cat who lingers too long.
The fog at {zoneName} swallows trails. You go in with a way out already chosen, and you do not chase a scent off the path.
You walk into {zoneName} knowing a cat can lose the day here. The paths lie, and you keep close to what you can still smell clearly.
Trails braid and fade at {zoneName}. Getting lost on this ground is not a small thing, so you keep your head.
You walk into {zoneName} knowing this ground can hurt you, and you watch every approach.
The land here does not forgive a careless step. You go in ready to move.
Your fur tightens as you enter {zoneName}. This is dangerous ground.
You step into {zoneName} as if every open stretch could throw a stick. Humans keep a camp here, and cats die on this kind of ground.
Fire-scent and upright tracks mark {zoneName} as human country. No cat can fight what lives here. You go in only as far as you must.
This is deadly ground: humans camp at {zoneName}, and their sharpened sticks wound from far off. You do not linger in the open.
You step into {zoneName} as a cat steps toward a clan's den-ground. Hyenas keep this place, and they will not give way for you.
The den-smell at {zoneName} is thick enough to taste. A hyena clan holds this ground, and cats have come off it the worse.
This is deadly ground: hyenas den at {zoneName}, and a clan will take your meal, or turn on you if you stay.
You step into {zoneName} as if the bear already knows. This is its ground, and cats die here.

A short-faced bear holds this place. You do not wander, and you do not compete with it for a meal.

A pack hunts {zoneName} as if it were their run. You go in only as far as you must, and you keep a way out.
This is deadly ground: wolves own the trails at {zoneName}, and they will not share them.
The snow above {zoneName} looks as if it has already chosen a cat. You cross only if you must, and you do not speak.
You step into {zoneName} under a slope that can bury you. This ground has taken cats, and it will take more.

The ice at {zoneName} is a killing thing. You keep off it if there is any other path, and you do not trust a clear stretch.
You step toward {zoneName} as cats did before the Breaking, and you remember how that ended. The ice here lies.

The tar at {zoneName} is a mouth in the ground. You go in only along the paths you trust, and you trust very little.
You step into {zoneName} as a cat steps around a trap. The seeps have taken hunters, and the stink of that is still here.
This is deadly ground: the tar at {zoneName} does not let go, and a wrong paw will cost you.
The stone at {zoneName} wants to come down. You cross the cut only if you must, and you do not look up for long.
You step into {zoneName} under walls that have killed. A wrong sound, a wrong pause, and the rock answers.
This is deadly ground: the cliffs at {zoneName} throw stone, and there is little room to be out of the way.
The water at {zoneName} is a wide, moving thing, and the old paths are gone. You go in only if the high ground still holds.
You step toward {zoneName} as if the river were hunting. A flood like this has drowned cats, and it will not make an exception for you.
This is deadly ground: the flood at {zoneName} cuts off a retreat, and the current does not care who you are.
The cold at {zoneName} is a killing cold. You step in only if you have a way to get out of the wind, or you do not stay.
You enter {zoneName} as if the air itself were the hunter. Cats have stiffened on this kind of ground.
This is deadly ground: the cold at {zoneName} does not ease, and a night in the open may be enough.

You enter {zoneName} as a cat enters a place that cannot feed you. Stay long, and the hunger will do the rest.

You enter {zoneName} as a cat enters a place that swallows directions. Cats who wander here do not always wander out.

You step into {zoneName} as a cat steps toward a killing place, slow and ready.
This ground has taken cats before. You do not wander on it.
Every scent at {zoneName} says the same thing: be ready, or do not come.

features._note: The player learns a feature by visiting, by scent, or from gossip (map 10.3; Director: exact camps and dens are not common knowledge). These are discovery and return beats, not Lore Book entries and not region arrivals. Gossip is narrator framing of what {sourceName} told the player, and it always names {zoneName}. Repeat visits assume the feature is already known. Neither feature moves, and neither can be claimed away.

variants.text: Smoke hangs over {zoneName} in a way no grass fire does. Upright figures move at the edge of a camp, and sharpened sticks lean waiting. This is a human camp, and no cat can fight what lives here.
You come upon a human camp at {zoneName}: fire, strange upright scent, and sticks honed to bite from far off. The ground around it is trodden in a way no pride would tread. You do not walk closer.

At {zoneName} you find what the far-edge stories meant. Humans keep a camp here, with fire and piled sticks, and their scent is nothing like a beast's. You watch from cover, and you leave yourself a way out.
A sharp fire-scent is on the ground at {zoneName}, mixed with a smell no beast leaves. Upright walkers have been here, and the smell of a camp clings to the earth.
You read the earth at {zoneName} and come up with smoke, strange hides, and the dry smell of honed wood. Humans have made a camp on this ground.
The scent at {zoneName} is fire and upright walkers, thick enough to be a living place, not a passing trail. There is a human camp here, or just off the next rise.
{sourceName} talks of fire and upright walkers at {zoneName}, and of sticks that wound from far off. A human camp, {sourceName} calls it, and says no cat should go in close.
{sourceName} came in from the far edges with a tight look, and said humans have made a camp at {zoneName}. They keep fire there, and they throw sharpened sticks.
{sourceName} warns you off {zoneName}. Upright walkers have settled there, {sourceName} says, with smoke by day and a camp that does not move.
The human camp is still at {zoneName}. Smoke still stains the air, and the upright walkers still keep to their ground.
You come back to {zoneName} and find the camp where it was. The fire-scent has not left, and neither have they.
The camp at {zoneName} has not moved. Humans still walk upright among their sticks and their fire, and you give them the same wide space as before.
The stink of many scavengers thickens into a den-smell at {zoneName}. Tracks overlap, and old bones lie cracked where a clan has fed. Hyenas keep this place, and they will take a meal if they can.
You find a hyena den at {zoneName}. The ground is packed by many paws, rank and sour, and the clan-scent is heavy enough to taste. You do not bring a meal any closer than you must.

At {zoneName} the scavenger-scent gathers at a den. Hyenas have worn this ground bare around it, and a whole clan could rise out of that stink. You keep your meal, if you are carrying a catch, and you keep moving.
A thick den-smell of hyenas is soaked into the earth at {zoneName}. This is not a passing track. A clan lives on this ground.
You read the earth at {zoneName} and come up with sour scavenger-scent, layered thick, and the greasy smell of old bones. Hyenas have a den here.
The scent at {zoneName} is a hyena clan at home: many overlapping trails, musk, and cracked marrow. Their den is close.
{sourceName} says hyenas have a den at {zoneName}, a sour place packed with tracks, and that a clan will take a meal from under you if you hunt there.
{sourceName} came back from {zoneName} still shaking the stink out of {sourceName}'s coat, and said a hyena clan dens there.
{sourceName} warns you that {zoneName} is hyena ground now. Their den is there, {sourceName} says, and they do not share a meal.
The den-smell is still heavy at {zoneName}. The hyena clan has not left.
You come back to {zoneName} and find the den where it was. The tracks are fresh, and the stink has not faded.
The hyenas still keep their den at {zoneName}. You give it the same space as before, and you do not eat in the open here.

territory_gossip._note: Spoken (or narrator-framed) news when a region changes hands, is claimed from the wild, is lost, goes wild, or becomes contested. Every entry is kind holder_change, matching the shared fact-kind list. sociability is the teller's band; baseline is the unbanded default for that change and side. side is set only for news about the player's pride. leaderKnown lines use {name} as a known leader or the cat who marked the ground, and must not fire without one. For contested news, {holderName} is the current holder and {rivalName} is the challenging pride (the same token as the My Pride contested header). {loserName} is the pride that lost the ground. {prideName} is the player's pride.
